Never had we seen a US election prolonged as much as the current one. Our chart today look into the distribution of electoral votes by each state. Theoretically, the votes are to be allotted by the population of each state. However, we found out that it is not precisely the case. For example, Montana has almost two times the population of Wyoming, but both states hold 3 votes. Another example, Wisconsin and Colorado both have a population of 5.8m but the former has 1 more vote than the latter. 

Part of the reasons is that the votes are calculated by The Method of Equal Proportions using the 2010 Census population data. The population of each state has changed drastically since then, hence the disproportion. The next Census happens during 2020 but will only impact the votes in the 2024 election.

Another interesting fact, theoretically a presidential candidate only needs to win in the 11 most populated states to win overall. Happy Saturday!

Over the weekend, we heard that Sean Connery, the actor of the first Jame Bond movies, had passed away. That why we want to create a post in commemoration of his work. 

James Bond is one of the most long-lasting film series in film history. The main character, Bond, is a British secret agent working for MI6 who also answers to his codename, 007. Until now, a total of 7 actors had played the role James Bond, but only 6 of them were recognised. Due to a poor match with the audience's expectation of James Bond and the fact that Sean Connery had set a very high bar, David Niven's James Bond was widely criticised and hardly accepted.

Because Connery was so favoured by the audiences, he was bought back several times after retiring from Bond films, including playing in Diamonds Are Forever in 1971 and Never Say Never Again in 1983. He was hence made the longest-lived James Bond.

If you have time, we recommend you to rewatch some of the classic James Bond films! They are so cool!

Our first covid post. Today, we want to look at restaurants during covid. The chart shows the number of reservations each day in 2020 compared to the same day in 2019. The progress of recovery is very different between countries: Australia and Germany are almost fully recovered; recovery in UK and Ireland did not sustain; the situation in the American continents are gradually improving but still rather poor.

In the UK, the government launched the Eat Out to Help Out scheme which had successfully incentivised many people to visit restaurants. On 31st August, the supposed last day of the scheme, restaurant reservations even surge to a 100% increase compared to 2019. The scheme did not fully withdraw after August, but the impact of the stimulus is not as strong as before.

Restaurants obviously took a massive hit during covid. What do you think restaurants can do to save themselves? Share your thought!

People would image the world is getting better and better with development in both the economy and technology. The truth is that developed countries are facing more serious problems with homeless people than ever. The chart presents the record and estimations of homeless people in different countries. As we can see, US, Germany and France have the largest homeless population, worse than some less developed countries such as Brazil and Mexico. In Germany, the actual number of homeless could be 800K, more than double the number in the chart, as we don't consider refugees in this count.

One common misconception we want to demystify is that people often mistook homeless people with rough sleepers, people who sleep on the street. The truth is a substantial proportion of homeless people live under at places with a roof. Rough sleepers are only a kind of homeless.

So what do you think are the root causes of increasing homeless people? And what role should the governments play in solving the issue? Share your thoughts!

Last weekend, we did a survey to see how many people think they are funnier than the average person. Interestingly, 59% of people think they do better than average. Daniel Kahneman, noble prize launderette and author of 'Thinking, Fast and Slow', pointed out in his book that people tend to think they are better than the average, a psychology phenomenon so-called illusory superiority. The reason behind is that people realise the external traits and circumstances that guide other people's actions, but when it comes to themselves, they tend to think it's all about their intention, effort, desire and agency.

Talking about humour, there is also a stereotype that men are funnier than women. According to a research reference on BBC, 63% of men were funnier than the average woman. The researcher explained, 'the whole thing is not about 'women are not funny'... It's just that on average we find there's a difference.".He further explained that evidence suggests humour plays a "major role in mating": women tend to look for a sense of humour in a partner as it is "strongly correlated with intelligence"; men, on the other hand, prefer women who laugh at their humour.

So do you agree that the average man is funnier than the average woman? No stigma attached!

The idea of promoting green energy first started in 1970s, however after 50 years of global effort, only 7% of the world's energy consumed is currently produced by renewables. Within renewables, hydropower and nuclear power are the largest sources, contributing to 2.7% and 1.8% of world energy consumption respectively. Other sources such as biofuel, wind and solar are insignificant (each below 1%). If the world progresses at the same pace, we are not likely to see green energy fully replacing oil and gas in the 21st century.

It may seem like we have little influence on how energy is produced, but our actions can actually help change the landscape. How about starting from using less one-time plastic products, such as plastic bags, boxes and straws?

Dating apps are often being viewed as tools for hookups. We found out that this is only partly true. 52% of users actually don't hook up with their dating app connections. Another report by Business of Apps states that over 70% of Tinder users never meet up with anyone they knew from the app. It is unclear, for people who never had a one night stand, whether they don't want a hookup or they never had a chance to do so.

However, we do see meaningful relationships happening on dating apps. Many users engage in long term relationships, of which 13% end up getting married/engaged. If you are looking for a stable and permanent relationship, dating apps are still a valuable channel.

And if you are using dating apps and want to present yourself appealingly, our chart suggests some biggest turn-off when people view profile pictures. Another important concept to bare in mind is that the traits are not binary but are measured over a spectrum. In other words, a person who is marginal more introvert is considered as introvert, but it doesn't mean the person is always shy and less communicative. Nothing is better than Saturday beer, except Saturday beer in Prague. In Czech, beer is cheaper than water! You can buy a pint at the price of $1.6 whereas a bottle of water would cost more than $2.

To protect their market share in such a vast market, large breweries keep their margin low to push out small breweries. Published in 2006, the book The Female Brain made a claim that women are chatterboxes, speaking an average of 20,000 words per day, nearly three times the 7,000 spoken by men. 

Finding the claim hard to believe, researchers at the University of Texas at Austin's psychology department conducted their own research. They used a device to collect data on the chatter patterns of 396 university students (210 women and 186 men) at colleges in Texas, Arizona and Mexico. IThe average number of words spoken by the majority of men and women were about the same: women at 16,215 words and men at 15,669. However, the researchers pointed out that women tend to jaw more about other people, whereas men are apt to hold forth on more concrete objects.

Do you think women actually speak more than men? Discuss.

Fascinating data story. In WW2, the survival rate of The Allies’ airmen had been as low as 41%. Reducing air battle causalities became a pressing issue. The command came up with a solution to arm their bombers more heavily. In order to find out which parts should be armed with additional armour, the bullets holes of the returned air-planes were assessed. Data showed that damages mainly concentred in three areas: the fuselage, the outer wings and the tail. Placing extra layer of metals on three areas would seem to be the obvious answer. However, Abraham Wald, a statistician, pointed out a critical flaw in the conclusion: the analysis only took samples from returned planes. He explained that if a plane makes it back safely after being shot, it means the bullets didn’t damage the most critical parts. Reinforcement is instead needed on the sections that had few bullet holes, such as the engines and the cockpit, as planes that were hit in those sections probably never made it back. The finding eventually helped to turn the tide of the war.
